newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 index rebounds in more active trading.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 index rebounds in more active trading.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 and RPIX indices broke free from a run of losing sessions to post moderate gains on Monday in heavier activity.
The PX50 gained 1.6 points to 575.4 -- its first rise in five sessions -- while the RPIX index of continuously traded shares was up six points at 1,165.
Some of the major issues moved ahead strongly with Komercni Banka jumping 27 crowns to 2,398, Ceska Sporitelna rising seven crowns to 352 and CEZ up five crowns to 1,048.
The PSE's most heavily capitalised issue SPT Telecom, though, failed to show any signs of a rebound, falling five crowns to 3,372.
But dealers said the share's recent performance should be put into the context of its strong performance throughout the last 12-months during which time it has risen from a low of just 2,210.
Seen in this light, they said, SPT was a strong performer with a bright long term future.
"The perception of the market is that SPT is not going to outperform the market in the next few days...its a long term buy rather than short term," said Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.
Among the broader issues, glass fibre maker Vertex was again the biggest loser falling 234 crowns to 4,455.
